scores.evidence: Yjs CRDT with the y-prosemirror binding. The server relays and stores edits but does not decide their order
scores.rationale: Accurate on Yjs, relative positions, awareness, UndoManager and commit-before-confirm; minor imprecision such as Yjs snapshot+log equality checks and unproven claims about old clients deleting unknown nodes, no major errors.
Covers core sync, persistence, authz, scale, and features with explicit deferrals; rich-text merge edge semantics and offline are only thinly addressed.

scores.evidence: Permissions and metadata favour consistency: Postgres is the source of truth
scores.rationale: Consistent ownership and choices; slight tension between Redis pub/sub multi-node and in-memory per-doc state and the revocation push path is lightly specified.

scores.evidence: 0 divergent final states over 10,000 sessions ... 0 confirmed edits lost over 1,000 injected faults
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to the riskiest assumptions, run first (V1/V2 before real content), labeled as assumptions, and continues in production via state hashes and V5.

scores.evidence: Each one changes the phase order if it is false
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled, unknowns are flagged with owners and deadlines, and the plan says what changes if each is wrong.

scores.evidence: Fault-injection durability suite ... Revocation pushed to the sync nodes, which disconnect or downgrade the user
scores.rationale: Covers crashes, failover, divergence, tenant leaks, old clients, noisy tenants, Redis loss and content leakage with detection and recovery; adversarial CRDT payloads and malformed updates are less detailed.

scores.evidence: A GitHub Actions pipeline builds each container image once and moves it from staging to production ... Redeploy the previous image
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, SLO burn-rate alerts, on-call, DR drills and migrations are covered; incident ownership details and team size are somewhat thin.

scores.evidence: Cost per active editor per month | UNKNOWN. Product/finance supplies it
scores.rationale: Identifies cost measurement and build-vs-buy, storage bound and cost checks, but offers no estimate of drivers (memory per doc, connections, Redis fan-out) and defers cost to an unknown.

scores.evidence: R3: every stored doc and the wire protocol take this format
scores.rationale: Explicit reversibility ratings per decision, points of no return, early validation of the hard ones, and stated fallback and exit paths.

scores.evidence: ≤ 4 runtime components (web/API, sync, Postgres, Redis) plus object storage, with one on-call rotation
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with an explicit complexity budget; a formal pen-test gate, many phases and a separate dependency-kind taxonomy add some ceremony.

scores.evidence: Tasks (widest rework first) ... Exit check: V1 and V2 pass
scores.rationale: Concrete phased tasks, dependency-driven ordering, checkable exit criteria, a thin first slice, and explicit fallback/re-plan actions when checks fail.

checklist.evidence: Yjs CRDT with the y-prosemirror binding ... V1 finds a divergence ... → Automerge or a server-sequenced OT design
Seeded fuzz harness: 2–20 simulated clients making random edits, with reordering, duplication, delay, partitions and offline/reconnect
Append-only Yjs update log plus compacted snapshots in Postgres ... confirms an edit only after the commit
Hocuspocus Redis extension (pub/sub): any node can serve any doc ... jittered backoff
The client keeps unconfirmed edits in IndexedDB and resends them on reconnect
checks permissions when the connection opens and on every message ... Revoked users disconnected within 5 s
Per-user undo (Y.UndoManager) ... A restore is applied as a new edit, so history only moves forward
Yjs awareness, temporary and never stored
Phase 1: Data contracts and the correctness core ... Phase 4: Collaboration features
50 concurrent editors, 500 viewers ... Evict idle docs from memory; batch commits per doc
The protocol version and the minimum client version are checked when the connection opens; clients below it are read-only

traps.evidence: Adopt open source and run it ourselves: Yjs, TipTap/ProseMirror, Hocuspocus
Phase 1: Data contracts and the correctness core
The server confirms an edit only after the commit.
Customers accept that a revoked user keeps the copy already synced to their device

note: Strong, risk-ordered plan that proves the CRDT sync core and durability first and names its decisions and unknowns; weaker on rich-text merge semantics, undo and large-doc detail, and cost estimation.
